standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic scope and permission task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With a need already identified, the learner writes out a clear, specific plan for what helping would actually involve, then sits down with the adults in their household to walk through that plan and ask for real permission before doing anything involving people, spaces, or resources outside the learner's own immediate control.
safetyNotes: Do not begin any part of this project that involves people, spaces, or resources outside your own immediate control until a trusted adult in your household has given real permission.
Do not contact anyone outside your household on your own to plan or arrange this project — any outside contact happens through or alongside a trusted adult.

simulationAlternative.description: If the specific project cannot get real permission from a trusted adult this week, the learner instead writes out the full scope-and-permission conversation as a rehearsal — what they would say, what questions or concerns a trusted adult might raise, and how they would respond — without holding the real conversation yet.

materials: learner-local: the need identified on the previous lesson day

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one concern a trusted adult raised that you had not thought of yourself, and how it changed, or confirmed, your plan.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Scope specificity: The written scope names a specific action, a realistic timeframe, and every other person involved. | Permission process: A real permission conversation with a trusted adult is documented, including whether permission was granted, granted with changes, or not yet given. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write a short backup plan for what they would do if a trusted adult approved the need but restricted the scope, so they have already thought through a smaller version of the project.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic scope and permission task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

localMaterials.label: the need identified on the previous lesson day
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: scope and permission worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With a need already identified, the learner writes out a clear, specific plan for what helping would actually involve, then sits down with the adults in their household to walk through that plan and ask for real permission before doing anything involving people, spaces, or resources outside the learner's own immediate control.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact scope and permission decision or action.
Model move 2: Before writing your plan, think about what an adult in your household would want to know before agreeing to a project like this.
Model move 3: Write a specific scope for the project: exactly what you would do, roughly how long it would take, where it would happen, and who besides you would be involved.

Model check: Scope specificity: The written scope names a specific action, a realistic timeframe, and every other person involved. | Permission process: A real permission conversation with a trusted adult is documented, including whether permission was granted, granted with changes, or not yet given.

resources.title: scope and permission action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for scope and permission.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: scope and permission coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a need already identified, the learner writes out a clear, specific plan for what helping would actually involve, then sits down with the adults in their household to walk through that plan and ask for real permission before doing anything involving people, spaces, or resources outside the learner's own immediate control.
Coach direction: Before writing your plan, think about what an adult in your household would want to know before agreeing to a project like this.
Learner prompt: List three questions you think a trusted adult in your household would ask about this project before saying yes.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: scope and permission complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Write a specific scope for the project: exactly what you would do, roughly how long it would take, where it would happen, and who besides you would be involved.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My scope names a specific action, not a vague goal like 'help out.'
Response 2 (t2-p2): My scope includes a realistic time estimate and names every other person who would be involved.

Equal-access rule: If the specific project cannot get real permission from a trusted adult this week, the learner instead writes out the full scope-and-permission conversation as a rehearsal — what they would say, what questions or concerns a trusted adult might raise, and how they would respond — without holding the real conversation yet.

resources.title: scope and permission minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one concern a trusted adult raised that you had not thought of yourself, and how it changed, or confirmed, your plan.

Success checks: Scope specificity: The written scope names a specific action, a realistic timeframe, and every other person involved. | Permission process: A real permission conversation with a trusted adult is documented, including whether permission was granted, granted with changes, or not yet given.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: scope and permission supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional scope and permission condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Scope specificity: The written scope names a specific action, a realistic timeframe, and every other person involved. | Permission process: A real permission conversation with a trusted adult is documented, including whether permission was granted, granted with changes, or not yet given..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain one concern a trusted adult raised that you had not thought of yourself, and how it changed, or confirmed, your plan.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Scope specificity: The written scope names a specific action, a realistic timeframe, and every other person involved. | Permission process: A real permission conversation with a trusted adult is documented, including whether permission was granted, granted with changes, or not yet given.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u06-l02-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
